# CharterMesh

CharterMesh is a provider-neutral organization-as-code control plane for AI
work.

When asked to apply this repository to another project, read BOOTSTRAP.md and
use its inspect -> plan -> exact human approval -> apply -> verify protocol.
With only the GitHub URL, the package-ready entry point is
`npx --yes github:jade-blanco/chartermesh#v0.0.10-alpha.1` after package-download
approval. The GitHub form requires Git, npm lifecycle scripts for the
dependency-free prepare build, and normal network access. The tag selects a
version but is movable and is not a cryptographic commit attestation.
The v0.0.10-alpha.1 package includes project-type templates, TEAM-CHARTER,
one-plan kickoff --host, and reviewed project customization. A source checkout
is optional. The default generated MCP command targets the same tag; require
approved apply and the new-session MCP health gate before reporting host-bound
setup complete. Omit --host when the provider-neutral core is wanted.
Tool execution is governed by OrgSpec allowlists, relative workspace roots,
exact-call human approvals, evidence hashes, and bounded iterations.
Any local executable can connect through the shell-free command-process JSON
contract; its approved executable digest is pinned and it runs from a dedicated
cwd. Unknown model cost follows the user's OrgSpec policy and is never silently
zero. Allowlisted audit export and DB+artifact backup/restore remain local.
Runtime JSON is schema-validated before inference. Model calls are recorded
before start and share durable CLI/dashboard/signal cancellation. Work lists
support cursors and archive, audit export streams, outbox delivery retries and
dead-letters, and optional local schedules are disabled by default and start
zero models on an empty queue.
Decision Packet v1alpha2 separately binds exact artifact bytes/media type and
the canonical producer-report sidecar. Producer-reported checks remain
claimed, including in experimental runtime_compiled mode. Human decision
surfaces must show the exact bounded artifact preview as well as the packet;
the projection is not a substitute for the deliverable. SQLite schema v15
stores report identity, AgentHost lineage, exact actor/request idempotency, and
governed change-set reservation/settlement state. runtime_compiled is currently a
BuiltInManagedRunner API option, not a CLI/runtime.json setting.
Approved bootstrap plans also install six provider-neutral Apache-2.0 Agent
Skills, including `organization-bootstrap` and
`tool-grounded-implementation`. External MCP servers remain
uninstalled and disabled. Optional
SearXNG web.search requires a reviewed HTTPS/loopback endpoint, a tool-calling
engine, an OrgSpec allowlist entry, and exact per-query human approval.

For installed-project customization, read project-config --target PATH --json.
configure-project accepts optional --preferences-file and --organization-file,
previews without target writes, and applies only when the same options include
a human-approved exact --approve HASH. The six-field contract
chartermesh.dev/project-preferences/v1alpha1 includes apiVersion, language
auto|ko|en, approvalDetail eli5|concise|technical, tone plain|formal,
projectInstructions, and roleInstructions. preferences.json stores approved
advisory guidance; PREFERENCES.md is its readable projection. Neither changes
permissions, trains a model, or becomes a task ledger. ELI5 remains the default;
explicit presentation choices never remove hashes, evidence status, risks, or
unknowns. Decision Packet views honor language/detail preferences; auto means
CLI English and dashboard Korean. Bootstrap/configuration/evaluation plan
explanations remain English ELI5. Tone and free-form instructions guide models,
not translation of fixed UI labels or historical artifacts.
An OrgSpec candidate keeps metadata.id and uses exactly the next revision. It
must preserve current approval policy and existing execution/capability/
orchestration bindings. Active runs or in_progress work block customization;
other unfinished work must retain valid roles and targets, and the relevant
work-state hash is bound into the plan. Connections and schedules stay separate.
Even proposed/paused schedules protect referenced role/workflow definitions
against changes other than display names. Native projection refresh supports
one existing Codex or Claude host, requires matching --host codex|claude and
--executable-sha256, and additionally
--allow-unrestricted-read for Codex. Multiple hosts fail closed; removed roles
become retired notices. Verify a new host session after apply. Applied
customization prevents ordinary bootstrap overwrites; preserve preferences in
bootstrap/kickoff and connection changes. A coordinator may propose
improvements but never approves itself.

Use a no-candidate configure-project plan to refresh an installed project's
version pins and managed guides while preserving its organization, preferences,
and unrelated user text; never use bootstrap as a customization reset. A pending
configuration marker and the exact approved plan are atomically committed to
Control Plane metadata before file replacement. Work mutations remain blocked
across a crash until the same plan resumes. Organization drift makes old MCP
and dashboard sessions reject mutations and require a restart; read-only
inspection and preference-only read refresh remain available.

Fresh projects can use one approved kickoff plan for a provider-neutral team,
work allocation, copy/paste handoffs, human approval rules, files, the project
brief, acceptance criteria, and the first WorkItem. Optional `--host codex` or
`--host claude` projects project roles plus a local stdio MCP bridge in that
same plan; `configure-host` remains available for later changes. Each bridge process
has a unique non-human actor and exact WorkItem/Run/Attempt/lease/generation
fences; it has no approval authority. Projected roles request one bounded,
content-addressed multi-file change set, then a separately controlled human
reviews its stored bytes and approves the exact call and Decision Packet. A new
claim can apply only that stored set through a recoverable transaction.
Before a host-bound kickoff may start even a version probe, bind the observed
host executable SHA-256. When the digest option is omitted, kickoff reports the
observed value and exits without starting the host; repeating with that digest
still produces one plan and one CharterMesh human approval. Codex project trust
or Claude's one-time MCP permission is a separate host UI action, not a second
CharterMesh approval. After apply, close the old host session, start a new
trusted session from the project root, and require
`chartermesh_status` plus `chartermesh_work_next` to pass before assigning work.
Provider-native parent permissions can override projected child defaults, and
`human:*` is a procedural local policy boundary rather than cryptographic proof
against a process with CLI/database access. This pre-alpha is not a production
authorization or OS-sandbox system.

One project MCP bridge serves the aggregate allowed role set. Generated agents
must claim only their own `ownerRole`, but native subagent identity is not
authenticated at the shared bridge, so cross-role separation is procedural.
Kickoff creates one initial operator-owned WorkItem. Coordinator and verifier
stages are bounded copy/paste consultations unless the Control Plane separately
assigns role-owned WorkItems; they must not claim or mutate the operator item.

The evaluate-decision-review command is dry by default. Its live mode requires
the exact plan hash and an attested Codex executable/model binding for 20
stateless calls over the fixed ten-case raw/decision_review suite. The plan
also binds the exact local harness-source digest and the live runner compares
the complete regenerated plan before starting. Fatal identity, executable, or
unsettled-process failures stop the study. The result is descriptive proxy
regression evidence only, never human, causal, statistical, approval, or
autonomy evidence.
Quota/rate capacity and authentication boundaries pause this benchmark after
the child settles, without scoring the attempted call. An operator signal is
resumable only between calls; Ctrl+C during an active model call leaves an
unknown outcome and fails closed. Each invocation is durably marked before
launch, and running, failed, active, or unknown attempts are never retried
automatically. A clean paused checkpoint lives only under
`.chartermesh/evaluations/<benchmarkId>/checkpoint.json`; the final report
alone is written to exports. Resume is a dry
`--resume --account-context same|changed|unknown` plan followed by a fresh
exact `RESUME_PLAN_HASH` approval. The completed prefix is immutable and the
model, executable/hash, limits, suite, protocols, and source digest must still
match. No account/email/auth-path/credential fingerprint is stored; context is
operator-declared and unverified. Every resume creates a new segment and
confounds a strict uninterrupted reviewer-benefit claim; changed or unknown
also discloses account-continuity uncertainty. Source changes invalidate old
plan hashes.
Each resumed segment binds its source checkpoint, prior segment chain, attempt
count, and approval hash; an exclusive used-approval receipt is written before
the next model process. Dead-owner stale-lock recovery is allowed only for the
exact clean paused state. State-path symlink/junction components are rejected.
These are single-user local hash controls, not signatures or protection from a
malicious local writer or whole-directory rollback.
